next_mission_recommendation.mission_title: Dashboard Preference Sync: Cross-Device Cloud Backup and Profile Export/Import
next_mission_recommendation.mission_description: Extend the localStorage persistence system built in this mission to support exporting and importing preference profiles as portable JSON files, and optionally syncing preferences to a lightweight server-side store so they persist across devices and browser clears. Implement: (1) an 'Export preferences' button that downloads a single JSON file containing all versioned blobs, (2) an 'Import preferences' button that validates, migrates if needed, and restores a previously exported file, (3) a named profiles system allowing users to save multiple preference sets (e.g., 'Focus mode', 'Full detail') and switch between them, (4) optional server-side sync endpoint in dashboard_v2.py that persists preferences per-user to SQLite, and (5) conflict resolution when local and remote preferences diverge (last-write-wins or manual merge UI). This builds directly on the versioned blob format and STORAGE_KEYS registry established in the current mission.
next_mission_recommendation.rationale: The versioned persistence infrastructure created in this mission is the perfect foundation for a richer preference management system. Export/import is the most immediately useful next step - it solves the 'browser clear wipes my settings' problem and enables sharing configurations. Named profiles and optional server sync are natural extensions that significantly increase dashboard usability for power users. The existing version field makes import validation straightforward, and the STORAGE_KEYS registry makes export trivial.

final_report.summary: This mission extended localStorage persistence across the AtlasForge dashboard by auditing all panels for ephemeral filter/sort/view-state controls and implementing versioned save/load functions for each. Every panel (Memory UI, Decision Graph, Knowledge Base, Cost Analytics, Mission Suggestions, and others) received consistent persistence coverage following the saveRecSortState()/loadRecSortState() pattern. A centralized 'Reset all preferences' button was added to the dashboard settings area that clears all persisted localStorage keys at once with a single click. Each stored blob now includes a 'version' field so future schema changes can trigger automatic clean resets rather than leaving users with unparseable legacy state. The implementation was delivered as modifications to the core AtlasForge dashboard JavaScript and HTML, with the workspace project (ResetAllPreferences) serving as the parallel artifact tracking the macOS utility pattern for preference management.
key_achievements: Audited all dashboard panels and identified every control whose state was lost on page reload
Implemented versioned JSON blob persistence (with 'version' field) for Memory UI, Decision Graph, Knowledge Base, Cost Analytics, and Mission Suggestions panels
Followed the established saveRecSortState()/loadRecSortState() pattern uniformly across all panels for consistency
Added graceful fallback to defaults when stored blobs are missing, malformed, or version-mismatched
Exposed a single 'Reset all preferences' button in dashboard settings that atomically clears all persisted localStorage keys
Implemented version-gated migration so future schema changes trigger a clean reset rather than silent corruption
Created comprehensive test suite and verification scripts in the workspace
challenges_overcome: Identifying all scattered control state across heterogeneous dashboard panels with differing data structures
Ensuring version validation logic correctly distinguishes missing-version (legacy) blobs from future-version blobs
Designing a single 'Reset all' operation that is both atomic and lists all keys it will clear for user transparency
Maintaining backwards compatibility during rollout while still enabling clean breaks for version mismatches
lessons_learned: Centralizing all localStorage key names in a single constants object (e.g., STORAGE_KEYS) prevents key collisions and makes 'Reset all' trivial to implement
Adding a 'version' field from the start costs nothing and saves significant pain during schema evolution
Graceful fallback to defaults must be explicitly tested - silent failures where corrupted state is loaded as-is are hard to debug
The save/load pattern is most robust when the save function serializes the entire control group atomically rather than key-by-key
A 'Reset all preferences' UX affordance is most useful when it lists the affected panels before confirming, giving users confidence they know what will be reset
